$comment: Cairnet design tokens. Single source of truth for colour, type, spacing, canvas, mark geometry and motion. Read by Python (scripts/tokens.py) and by the Remotion project (import this file directly). Do not hardcode any value from this file anywhere else. See tokens.md for the reasoning and the open questions.

meta.units: Colours are hex. Type and spacing are ratios of canvas width unless the key ends in Px. Mark geometry is in the mark's own 200-unit grid. Motion is in milliseconds and in frames at 30fps.

neutral.$comment: Interface greys for the mockups inside the frames: panels, placeholder bars, inactive type. These already existed, unnamed, invented per script, which produced eleven values across five near-duplicate pairs. One value per rung now. Tailwind direction: 50 lightest, 950 darkest.

document.$comment: Print and PDF chrome for the brand mock and proposals. Deliberately separate from the post palette: these are page furniture on white paper, they never appear in a post asset, and they should not be reached for when building one.

semantic.$comment: What a colour is for. Reach for these in a build script, not for the primitives above. textOnDarkSubdued (Mist) is the middle tier on charcoal, added 2026-08-27: Stone at 4.72:1 is legible but reads dull for a line that carries meaning, and Off-White flattens any hierarchy it sits in. Mist is clearly subordinate and still bright. shadowOnDark added 2026-08-27: the Proof family's offset block was drawn as black at 35% over charcoal, which composites to #121213 -- a colour the brand had never declared, on a system whose own rule is palette-only. The depth device is deliberate and reusable, so it gets a name rather than an exemption. The value is exactly what it already composited to, so nothing re-renders.

contrast.$comment: Computed, not assumed. WCAG 2.1 ratios. Verified by scripts/tokens.py, which recomputes them from the hex values on import and fails if any drift. AA needs 4.5:1 for body text and 3.0:1 for large text and graphics.

rules.$comment: Signal fails AA for body text on both grounds: 3.43:1 on charcoal and 4.48:1 on off-White, the second missing 4.5 by a hair. It is a large-text and graphics colour only, on either ground, which is what the Teaching family already does by using it for the 112px number and nothing else. Slate is structural on charcoal and readable type on off-White; Stone is the reverse. Neither is legible as body text on both.

tiers.$comment: The mark's four stones, base first, rising to the blaze. Light grounds darken as the stack rises; dark grounds lighten. Charcoal is invisible on the charcoal band, so the reversed set is mandatory rather than a style choice.

mark.$comment: Mark B, locked 2026-08-13. (x, y, w, h) on the 200-unit grid, base stone first. geometry.py derives the lockup from these; do not restate them. centroidCorrection is how much of the optical-centring correction to apply where the mark stands alone or sits in a round crop: the stack is bottom-heavy, so its centre of mass sits below its box centre and exact box-centring reads as sagging. Half is deliberate -- the full correction crowds the blaze against the top edge. The offset itself is deliberately not stored here: it is computed from the rects above (8.9% of ink height, as it happens), so it stays true if the two known off-grid coordinates are ever regularised. Only the vertical is corrected; the horizontal wobble is the hand-stacked quality and is not an error to fix.

scale.$comment: How big the mark is drawn on a composed frame, as a ratio of canvas width. This is the one thing about the mark that the frame decides rather than the mark, so it is keyed per context -- there is no universal mark size and this object should not grow one. endCard 0.17593 is 190px at 1080 wide, which is exactly what the approved end card already draws, so adopting this token re-renders nothing. Added 2026-09-01: the Remotion project needed a mark size and found the only existing value in the system was a bare 190 sitting in build_end_card.py.

lockup.$comment: Inputs only. geometry.py computes the derived anchors by reading Poppins' real cap height rather than assuming it. descriptorSizeRatio RAISED 0.30 -> 0.42 on 2026-09-18, and descriptorDrop REPLACED by descriptorGap at the same time. At 0.30 the descriptor's tracking -- which is derived from the flush-right constraint, not chosen -- came out at 0.398em, so the line was tiny letters flung very far apart, and it collapsed at any real display size: 6.4px cap height in the site nav, which sets the lockup 176px wide. 0.42 is the largest size that keeps tracking inside the normal range for set caps (0.109em); 0.44 drops to 0.076em and AI INTEGRATION starts reading as one dense slab rather than a tracked descriptor. Nothing about the horizontal lockup's silhouette moves: it is still 461.54 x 118 with the same flush right edge, because the descriptor grows into tracking it was already occupying. descriptorGap is the reason this should not recur. The old descriptorDrop was the distance from the wordmark baseline to the descriptor baseline, which is a function of the descriptor's cap height -- so changing the size silently changed the gap between the two lines, and the two numbers had to be edited in lockstep by hand. descriptorGap is that gap itself, the clear space under the wordmark baseline, and geometry.py derives the drop as descriptorGap + descriptor cap height. 4.2 is exactly what 0.30/21.0 produced, so the relationship the lockup was locked with is preserved rather than re-chosen. Resize the descriptor now and the vertical takes care of itself.

type.$comment: Ratios of canvas width. At 1080 wide these reproduce the settled frames exactly, so adopting the tokens re-renders nothing. Several steps are near-duplicates that predate this file; see tokens.md, Open questions. claim was added 2026-09-03 for the Statement carousel: headline at 0.07037 was sized when five lines shared one frame, and a slide carrying two lines can hold far more. 0.08519 is 92px at 1080. Sized against the genuinely longest line, which is 'specific thing fixed.' on slide two, not 'Most businesses' on slide one: at 96px the first fits and the second ran 31px past the margin. A genuinely new step rather than another near-duplicate: the nearest existing are 76px and 112px, and 112 overflows. Leading is two values -- see type.leading.

family.$comment: Paths relative to this file, so every reader resolves them the same way on any machine. They used to be absolute Linux paths into /usr/share/fonts/truetype/google-fonts/, which was true only inside Cowork -- the Remotion project could not use them at all and the Python builders could not run outside that one sandbox. The two Poppins faces are vendored in brand/fonts/ and verified against what geometry.py reads off them (unitsPerEm 1000, sCapHeight 705 on Bold). No third typeface. document is Liberation Sans and stays an absolute path, which resolves inside Cowork and nowhere else; build_cairnet_mock_v4.py loads it by path through reportlab. This used to end "nothing outside Cowork renders it", which stopped being true on 2026-09-18 when build_docs.py began setting document body copy on a Mac. A renderer that asks for a family rather than a file reads type.face.document instead, and that is where the substitution is declared rather than being invented in a build script.

face.$comment: The same two faces named the way a browser needs them, because a browser loads a family and a weight, not a file path. Remotion reads this and resolves file against brand/fonts/; Python reads type.family and gets the same binaries. One set of files, two ways of asking for it.

document.$comment: The body face for documents and proposals, as a browser asks for it. A stack rather than one family, because unlike display and body there is no file to vendor: Liberation Sans is GPL+FE and installed on precisely one machine in this setup, and the face is document chrome that never appears in a post asset. Order is preference, not fallback-by-accident. Liberation Sans first so a machine that has it uses it. Then Helvetica, which is the Helvetica-class face the profile's type rule actually names. Then Arial, which is metrically what Liberation Sans was drawn to match, and which every Windows machine has. The PDF embeds a subset of whichever one resolves, so the output is portable even though the input is not. Added 2026-09-18: the stack was a literal in build_docs.py, which is the exact failure this file exists to prevent.

leading.$comment: Ratios of FONT SIZE. Two values, not one -- display type set two lines deep wants more air than a stack of body lines, and collapsing them once already made this file assert something untrue. BASIS CHANGED 2026-09-02. display was 1.24 against a different base: build_end_card.py multiplied it by PIL's textbbox bottom, which is the ink depth of the particular string being set. That made the end card's leading depend on its copy -- 'Your next move,' measures 91 because of the comma's descender while 'marked in stone.' measures 82 -- and it meant the same token produced 112.84px in Python and 96.42px in a browser, measured both ways. 1.46545 is 112.84 over the 77px Python sets, so the approved card is reproduced exactly and CSS lineHeight now means the same thing. body CONVERTED 2026-09-10, the same way and for the same reason. Under the old basis it was copy-dependent in exactly the way display was: 1.19 times PIL's ink bottom gives 47.60px on 'That is potential earnings for your business lost.' and 42.84px on 'Not all of those calls would have booked, but even', because the second line happens to have no descender. Nothing read the token, so there was no artifact to reproduce; the value comes instead from the leading the Teaching notes already ship at, 44px on a 30px face, which was living in layout.teaching.noteLeading as a ratio of canvas width. A line height is a ratio of font size, so it belongs here, and noteLeading is gone. Worth knowing and slightly awkward: corrected, body and display land within 0.1% of each other, so the reason originally given for keeping two values, that display two lines deep wants more air than a stack of body lines, is not what the frames actually do. They stay two tokens because display's 1.46545 is the number that reproduces the approved end card exactly and must not be rounded toward body's.

layout.$comment: Per-composition geometry: the measurements a specific asset needs that are not general spacing. Keyed per composition on purpose, the same way mark.scale is -- there is no universal gap between a mark and a tagline. Extracted 2026-09-01 from build_end_card.py, which held all of it as bare literals, which meant the end card could not have been rebuilt in Remotion from tokens alone.

endCard.$comment: Ratios of canvas width. Each resolves to the pixel the approved card already draws at 1080 wide -- 74, 56, 16, 118, 7, 4 -- under both truncation and rounding, so it reproduces whichever way a reader resolves it. The stored ratios are the resolved ones, not the numbers originally typed: the script wrote 0.0525 and 0.11 and then truncated them to 56px and 118px, so 56.7 and 118.8 were never what anyone approved, and a renderer that does not truncate would have drawn them. ruleHeight and ruleRadius were bare pixels in a file whose contract is ratios; at any other canvas width they would have stopped scaling with everything around them. Mark size is mark.scale.endCard, line spacing is type.leading.display, and the two type sizes are type.scale.tagline and type.scale.domainEndCard.

statement.$comment: The Statement family's frame, extracted 2026-09-03 from scripts/style_test_families.py, where it was bare literals in the same way the end card's spacing was. Ratios of canvas width. claimTop and blaze are offsets from the top of the frame; footerFromBottom is measured up from the bottom, because the type hangs from the top margin and the mark sits on the floor. domainLeft was removed 2026-09-03: the domain's distance from the mark is not a free number, it is the nesting rule from the lockup. The mark's right edge is stepped, so type beside it clears only the stones actually next to it rather than the widest point, and the gap is lockup.gapRatio times the type's cap height. Deriving it means the footer cannot drift from the lockup the way it already had. ledeGap is the space between a claim and the supporting line under it, added 2026-09-11 when the Statement carousels gained sublines. Same 44px the Teaching family puts under its headings, so the two families breathe alike. leading here is a ratio of FONT SIZE, matching type.leading; the script's 96 against a 76px face is 1.2632, which is tighter than display leading because a claim set four lines deep wants less air than a two-line tagline, not more.

teaching.$comment: The Teaching family's frame, extracted 2026-09-09 from scripts/style_test_families.py where it was bare literals, the same way the end card's and the Statement family's were. Ratios of canvas width, except headerLeading which is a ratio of font size like type.leading. Off-White ground, so the mark uses color.tiers.light and the domain is Slate: Stone is legible on charcoal and not here. noteFromBottom places the closing note against the bottom of the frame rather than letting the rows push it down. On the four-row slide the flowed version landed 66px inside the footer; positioning it from the floor makes its spacing deliberate and independent of how many rows sit above it. bigRowHeight is for the row carrying the number a slide exists to land. It stays in the run rather than being lifted out above the note, so the reader reaches it by reading down the column, and it earns its weight from size and colour instead of from position. rowsTop is where a row block hangs when a note holds the floor beneath it. When there is no note the block is not hung at all, it is centred between the header and the footer, computed in TeachingSlide.tsx rather than stored. That replaced a second token, rowsTopWithLede, on 2026-09-10. The token had been hand-tuned to centre one specific slide, which meant it reproduced that slide and generalized to none: the next Teaching slide with no note had a different row count and would have left 27% of the frame empty. The derived version lands within 1px of the hand-tuned one, which is the check that it was the same intention all along. The condition is the note, not the lede: a lede changes where the rows start only because it makes the header taller, and the flex column already accounts for that. totalGap and noteGap removed 2026-09-10: totalGap spaced a lifted total that no longer exists now that slide three's answer sits in the run like slide two's, and noteGap was never read by anything once the note was anchored from the floor. noteLeading went the same day, to type.leading.body, where a line height belongs: it is a ratio of font size, not of canvas width.

canvas.$comment: Build at Reels size and crop to feed, not the reverse.

motion.$comment: PROPOSED, not settled. A approved the end card concept (stones dropping base to blaze) and the craft notes; the specific frame counts and curves below are a first pass and are the thing to react to once it renders. Everything else in this file reproduces existing approved output.

easing.$comment: settleOvershoot was removed 2026-09-02. A cubic bezier can only overshoot once, which is a lurch rather than a settle -- a stone coming to rest ticks down through several diminishing contacts. That is a spring, so the stones now use motion.spring and these curves are for type only.

duration.$comment: minHoldMs is the floor for any state a viewer has to read on a phone at arm's length.

endCard.$comment: dropFromMarkRatio is how far above its resting place a stone starts, as a multiple of the MARK's rendered size -- changed from a multiple of canvas height 2026-09-02. At 0.6 of canvas height a stone fell 1152px in 8 frames, covering 555px in the first frame alone and arriving before the eye could read it as falling: a pop, not a placement. A drop should scale with the thing being dropped, not with the frame it happens in. Rhythm: three stones five frames apart, then a beat, then the blaze -- the trail marker earns the pause, and it takes longest to set. Tagline moved from f48 to f52 on 2026-09-02 so the card carries a pulse the sound can sit on: the blaze lands at f26.8, the tagline is unveiled at f52 and the domain at f78, which is three beats 26 frames apart. Four frames of type timing bought an even rhythm for the sign-off, and nothing else moved. Stone settle durations lengthened 2026-09-03 (14->20, blaze 22->30): the descent read as fast. Slowing the window slows the fall and the bounces together, which keeps the physics coherent -- a stone that falls slowly and then rattles quickly is not a stone. Stagger widened 5 -> 11 frames on 2026-09-03. The descent was slowed twice and the stagger was left alone, so the falls got longer while the landings stayed 0.167s apart: slow stones arriving at a fast tempo. The blaze start moved with them so it still lands after the third stone rather than on top of its bounces.

bounce.$comment: How a stone lands. A spring overshoots BELOW its resting place, which for a stacked cairn means passing through the stone underneath: the gap between the blaze and the third stone is only 7 units, so any overshoot worth seeing is an overlap. A real stone bounces UP instead, in hops that get smaller until it stops, and never goes below where it lands. restitution is the velocity kept per bounce, so hop height is restitution squared. Raised 2026-09-02: at 0.22 the hop was 7px and only the blaze read as bouncing at all, because it was the only stone given enough frames to show it. All four now carry the effect and the blaze is pushed past them, so the exaggeration reads as the blaze being the blaze rather than as the only stone that moves like stone. A bounce needs frames as much as it needs height, which is why the durations in the timeline moved with these. audibleContacts is how many of a stone's contacts actually make a sound. The visual always bounces; the audio need not. Firing all four put twelve impacts inside 18 frames with two landing on the same frame as the next stone's arrival, which fused into a thickened attack at the original speed and separated into audible echoes once the descent was slowed. A real stone coming to rest is nearly silent after the first bounce, so one is defensible as well as cleaner. Added 2026-09-03.

rock.$comment: Stones rock as they settle: one edge lifts while the other drops, back and forth, dying away. A stone set down on uneven stone does not simply stop, and the bounce alone made them arrive rather than come to rest. Rotation is about each stone's own centre, so it tips rather than swings, and it starts on that stone's first contact because a stone in the air does not rock. degrees is the first tilt, the largest. Amplitude decays exponentially and is also multiplied by (1 - progress) so it reaches exactly zero when the window closes; exponential decay alone left a degree of tilt at the end that snapped back to level. The blaze gets four times the tilt and nearly twice the window, because it is the stone the eye ends on. The lower three are deliberately smaller in ANGLE and still move further in PIXELS, since they are wider: 3.5 degrees on the 190px base is about 5.8px at its edge, where 15 degrees on the 80px blaze is 10.4px. Matching the angles would have made the big stones flail.

statement.$comment: One beat. The claim is already the whole content, so the motion only lets it land: the blaze wipes down to open the frame, the lines arrive in sequence, and the Signal phrase resolves last because it is the argument. Opacity only, no rise: a fade-and-float is anyone's and is banned, and the end card's type already arrives this way. PROPOSED 2026-09-03, judge it by watching.

rules.$comment: Machine-checkable constraints. tokens.py asserts the numeric ones; the rest are here so the Remotion project inherits them rather than rediscovering them. motionOnlyOnStateChange was retired 2026-09-01. It had already been revised out of skills/profiles/cairnet.md and the Remotion handoff on 2026-08-31, and this file was the last copy still asserting it -- which is the exact drift this file exists to prevent, found by the first thing built against it. Its replacement is not machine-checkable and does not pretend to be: the test is 'could this movement belong to any brand?', not 'did something change'. A stone settling with weight passes; a fade-and-float fails even when it does mark a state change. Confetti, drifting particles, swooshes and cartoon squash stay out for being borrowed, not for being lively.
